I am a quantitative methodologist and PhD student at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. My research bridges causal machine learning, multilevel modeling, and statistical decision theory to improve educational research and program evaluation. I develop and study methods that help applied researchers accurately identify heterogeneous treatment effects and conduct rigorous and cost-aware program evaluations.

## Education

-   PhD in Educational Psychology | Expected 2027 <br> [University of Wisconsin-Madison]{style='color:gray;'}

-   MS in Educational Psychology | 2024 <br> [University of Wisconsin-Madison]{style='color:gray;'}

-   BS in Interdisciplinary Studies | 2022 <br> [North Carolina State University]{style='color:gray;'}

## Interests

-   Causal inference
-   Causal machine learning
-   Heterogeneous treatment effects
-   Multisite randomized controlled trials
